messages.author: bcff0ef7c0f12cb0
messages.subject: Secr Analysis-Too Few Values Error
parts:
Good Afternoon,

I am new to using R /secr and I am currently running single session data analysis in secr to generate a basic density estimate. I have uploaded the captfile/traptfile and created the capthist without any errors. When I get to secr.fit and run the basic model of D~1 g0~1 sigma~1 , I receive this error: 

too few values session 1 to determine start; set manually or select different session with details autoini

Using the code autoini as set in the manual using my capthist file: autoini(capthist, mask, detectfn = 0, thin = 0.2, tol = 0.001, binomN = 1, adjustg0 = TRUE, ignoreusage = FALSE) I receive this error in return:

 Error: too few values for autoini

Looking further, I understand I can manually set the starting values (example: start = list(D = 1, g0 = 0.01, sigma = 10). 

I am wondering what is the best method to determine my starting values? I have tried a few different values and received different results. To find sigma, according to the manual, I followed the below step:

1. Find value of sigma that predicts the 2-D dispersion of individual locations (see RPSV).

2. Once I did this I produced a RPSV of  0.01096177. However when I compute this in R (start = list(D = 1, g0 = 0.01, sigma = 0.01)) it produces NA  in the density results. 

My apologies in advanced if this is a simple answer or I missed where to find the answer in the manual.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Secr Analysis-Too Few Values Error
parts:
Welcome!
There is something odd about your detector coordinates. For detector spacings in metres, RPSV is also in metres. 1cm? Perhaps you did not project lat long?
Murray

messages.author: bcff0ef7c0f12cb0
messages.subject: Re: Secr Analysis-Too Few Values Error
parts:
Thank you. I did re-check my coordinates and fixed this. They are now converted properly to UTM in metres. My average spacing between detectors is 740m.

I'm still having issues with producing starting values for D, g0, and sigma to get a density estimate. I still receive the same errors of too few values for initial secr.fit and autoini. 

For g0, should it always be set to 0.1? And for sigma, is RPSV the best calculation for sigma to use? When I re-calculated RPSV I received 1215.259 metres. The other I tried was MMDM and received 2103.377 metres. I also have a buffer of 1740 metres that I have to take into account for secr.fit as well. 

Thank you for your assistance.

Murray
